name: Orthogenysuchus
isnote: Grouped with Mourasuchus and Purussaurus by Brochu (1999); other studies call it a pristichampsid or a synonym of Pristichampsus.
sum: Eocene caimanine from the Willwood Formation of Wyoming, known from a single skull.
holotype: AMNH 5178 — a skull without the lower jaws, Willwood Formation, Wyoming.
material: Only the holotype; its sutures are hard to see, making comparisons difficult.
biology: If close to Mourasuchus and Purussaurus, it implies long ghost lineages, since it is about 30 million years older.
author: Mook 1924

sources.text: Mook, C. C. 1924. A new crocodilian from the Wasatch Beds. American Museum Novitates(137): 1–4.
